description: Individual-level change model. Change succeeds only when each affected person progresses through Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability and Reinforcement; the first element that is missing is where resistance appears.
best_for: Change readiness assessment per stakeholder group
Diagnosing adoption risk on a roadmap
Designing training and reinforcement in a change plan

steps.name: Awareness
steps.description: Of the need for change — why, why now, and what happens if nothing changes.

steps.name: Desire
steps.description: To participate and support the change — personal motivation and WIIFM.

steps.name: Knowledge
steps.description: Of how to change — new processes, roles, tools and behaviours.

steps.name: Ability
steps.description: To implement required skills and behaviours in day-to-day work.

steps.name: Reinforcement
steps.description: To sustain the change — recognition, metrics, corrective action.

pitfalls: Jumping to Knowledge (training) before Awareness and Desire are established
Scoring ADKAR for the organisation as a whole instead of per stakeholder group
No owner for Reinforcement after the project team disbands
sources: Hiatt, J. — 'ADKAR: A Model for Change in Business, Government and our Community' (2006)
